ITQAN:v4p336/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p336/r4.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v4p336/r4.claim: Al-Raghib says the final scripture gathers the fruit of earlier scriptures, whose laws were partly superseded and partly completed by Muhammad's law.
ITQAN:v4p336/r4.anchor: وقال الراغب إن الله تعالى كما جعل نبوة النبيين نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم مختتمة

BURSEVI:v10p375/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375/r11.claim: Min Allāh modifies the Messenger through an omitted adjective clause and reinforces the grandeur of his origin.
BURSEVI:v10p375/r11.anchor: {من الله} متعلق بمضمر هو صفة لرسول مؤكد لما أفاده التنوين من الفخامة الذاتية

BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r1.claim: The description “reciting” is another adjective of the Messenger; ṣuḥuf means sheets, the material on which writing is placed.
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r1.anchor: صفة أخرى {صحفا} جمع صحيفة وهي ظرف المكتوب ومحله من الأوراق

BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r2.claim: The sheets are pure, protected from falsehood and from being touched except by the purified.
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r2.anchor: {مطهرة} أي منزهة من الباطل لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه ومن أن يمسه غير المطهرين.

BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r3.claim: Al-Kāshifī glosses the sheets as purified pages free of lies and slander.
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r3.anchor: وقال الكاشفي) : صحيفهاى اكيزه از كذب وبهبان

BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r4.claim: Ascribing recitation to sheets is figurative: the Qurʾan confirms earlier sheets in the foundations of laws and rulings, so its recited content is treated as those sheets.
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r4.anchor: ما يتلوه الذي هو القرآن مصدقا لصحف الأولين مطابقا لها في أصولي الشرائع والأحكام

BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r5.claim: Al-Kāshifī says the Qurʾan is called sheets in honor of its status, though it gathers the secrets of all scriptures.
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r5.anchor: (قال الكاشفي) : قرآنرا صحف كفت براي تعظيم با آنكه جامع أسرار جميع صحفست

BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r6.speaker: عين المعاني
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r6.claim: ʿAyn al-Maʿānī says the pages are called sheets because they are laid one upon another.
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r6.anchor: قال في "عين المعاني" وسميت الصحف لأنها أصحف بعضها على بعض أي وضع

QASHANI:98:2-8/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:98:2-8/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:98:2-8/r1.claim: The Messenger is apposition to the proof; the purified pages are tablets of celestial intellects and souls, reached through detachment and free of natural, material, and human corruption, containing enduring, just foundations of the true religion.
QASHANI:98:2-8/r1.anchor: بدل من البينة أي: الحجة القائمة الواضحة

QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r3.claim: The messenger from God recites purified scrolls preserved from alteration by the disbelievers.
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r3.anchor: أي حتى يأتيهم رسول من الله يقرأ كتبا مطهرة عن تبديل الكفار

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3454/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3454/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3454/r1.claim: Qatada says the disbelievers would persist in their condition until the clear proof arrived: the Messenger reciting purified pages, namely the Qur'an praised in the best terms.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3454/r1.anchor: عن قتادة لم يكن الذين كفروا من اهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين قال : منتهين عما هم فيه حتى تاتيهم البينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r3.claim: It also praises the Quran for including what earlier revealed books contained and adding further merit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r3.anchor: تنويه بالقرآن وفضله على غيره باشتماله على ما في الكتب الإلاهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r1.claim: Earlier scriptures promised a messenger with a law and a book confirming previous revelation, evoking the Torah’s promise to put God’s words in his mouth, the Gospel’s promise to remind people of Jesus’ words, and the Quran’s statement of confirmation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r1.anchor: وفي هذا تذكير بغلطهم فإن كتبهم ما وعدت إلا بمجيء رسول معه شريعة وكتاب مصدق لما بين يديه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r2.claim: Al-Ghazali says Muhammad’s combined virtues reached the level of a miracle and his many miracles were exceptionally manifest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r2.anchor: قال حجة الإسلام في كتاب ( المنقذ من الضلال ) : ( إن مجموع الأخلاق الفاضلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r3.claim: “From God” modifies “messenger,” rather than forming a genitive construction, allowing “messenger” to take a tanwin that magnifies him.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r4.claim: “Reciting purified pages” is a second adjective or circumstantial clause and embeds praise of the Quran, since the promised messenger is not elsewhere described as reciting pages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r4.anchor: صفة ثانية أو حال ، وهي إدماج بالثناء على القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r5.claim: “Reciting” means repeating words without addition or omission, whether read from writing or memory, indicating that the Prophet reads the unchanged revealed wording aloud.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r5.anchor: إعادة الكلام دون زيادة عليه ولا نقص منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r6.claim: “Pages” are writing sheets of parchment, leather, or cloth; calling the revelation pages is prospective metonymy because God commanded it to be written, like “I see myself pressing wine.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r6.anchor: مجاز بعلاقة الأيلولة لأنه مأمور بكتابته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r7.claim: The wording implies that God commanded the Quran to be written on sheets and other materials such as shoulder blades, scraps, and stones; it is called a book because it is written and recited.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p476/r7.anchor: أن الله أمر رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بكتابة القرآن في الصحف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r1.claim: The transitive use of yatlu with suhuf is a familiar metonymy approaching literal usage: the Prophet recited what was written, though he recited from memory as an unlettered man.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r1.anchor: مجاز مرسل مشهور ساوى الحقيقة قال تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r2.claim: Figurative purity means the scripture's meanings are unambiguous and free of misleading content; it alludes to distortion and errors in some scriptures held by the People of the Book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r2.anchor: أي كون معانيه لا لبس فيها ولا تشتمل على ما فيه تضليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r3.claim: Kutub is the plural of kitab, a noun meaning what is written; the Quranic sheets contain the Quran, which encompasses the uncorrupted substance of earlier revelations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r3.anchor: والكتب : جمع كتاب ، وهو فعال اسم بمعنى المكتوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r4.claim: The Quran is the quintessence and gathered fruit of earlier scriptures; calling that fruit kutub is a partitive metaphor, and the books can mean Quranic parts or suras treated as books.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p477/r4.anchor: فالقرآن زبدة ما في الكتب الأولى ومجمع ثمرتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#4/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#4/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#4/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak and Qatada say the purified pages are the Qur’an in its written sheets; al-Hasan instead says they are heavenly pages.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#2/r1.claim: The Messenger is Muhammad; the purified pages are the Qur'an's contents, which he recited from memory rather than from a written book, and they are free from idolatry and falsehood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#2/r1.anchor: والرسول هاهنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ومعنى يتلو صحفا أي ما تضمنته الصحف من المكتوب فيها وهو القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r2.claim: Ubayy had questioned Ibn Masʿud’s differing recitation; the Prophet affirmed both, and Gabriel then conveyed permission to recite in up to seven modes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r2.anchor: كان قد أنكر على إنسان، وهو: عبد الله بن مسعود، قراءة شيء من القرآن على خلاف ما أقرأه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir explains that the Prophet recited this surah to Ubayy to communicate, confirm, and warn him, rather than to learn or review it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r3.anchor: قرأها عليه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قراءة إبلاغ وتثبيت وإنذار، لا قراءة تعلم واستذكار، والله أعلم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies the clear proof as the Qur’an and its messenger Muhammad, who recites it from purified heavenly scriptures.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r3.anchor: أي: هذا القرآن؛ ولهذا قال تعالى:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r4.claim: The purified scrolls are like the honored, elevated, purified pages held by noble and obedient scribes in 80:13–16.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r4.anchor: في صحف مكرمة مرفوعة مطهرة بأيدي سفرة كرام بررة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r6.claim: Qatadah says the messenger recalls the Qur’an in the finest manner and praises it in the finest terms.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r6.anchor: قال ابن جرير: أي في الصحف المطهرة كتب من الله قيمة: عادلة مستقيمة،

FARRA:v3p281/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p281/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p281/r6.claim: “A messenger from God” is an indefinite restarted sentence following the definite al-bayyina; Ubayy’s reading makes rasūlan accusative, detached from al-bayyina.
FARRA:v3p281/r6.anchor: نكرة استؤنف على البينة، وهي معرفة، كما قال: «ذو العرش المجيد، فعال لما يريد » وهي في قراءة أبي: «رسولا من الله» بالنصب

JISHUMI:v10p7496/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7496/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7496/r4.claim: The common reading has rasūl nominative as an appositive to the clear proof; Ibn Masʿūd's codex is reportedly accusative as an independent or circumstantial form.
JISHUMI:v10p7496/r4.anchor: قراءة العامة: (رسول) بالرفع بدلا من البينة، وروي أن في مصحف ابن مسعود: (رسولا) بالنصب

JISHUMI:v10p7497/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r2.claim: Tilāwa is recitation, and ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfa.

KASHSHAF:98:2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:98:2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:98:2/r1.claim: Rasul is an appositive to the clear proof; in ʿAbd Allah's reading it is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of that proof.
KASHSHAF:98:2/r1.anchor: و { رَّسُولٌ } بدل من البينة .   وفي قراءة عبد الله : «رسولا »

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r5.claim: Pages are sheets, purified of falsehood; writings in them are upright, expressing truth and justice.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r5.anchor: { صحفا } قراطيس { مطهرة } من الباطل { فيها كتب } مكتوبات

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r1.claim: One interpretation identifies the clear proof as the Quran.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, the proof is the Messenger, whose signs of prophethood are clear.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r2.anchor: الثاني : الرسول الذي بانت فيه دلائل النبوة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r3.claim: A third interpretation is the disclosure of the truth and appearance of proofs.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r4.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b's reading says the disbelievers had not ceased to be separated from the proof.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r4.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي بن كعب : ما كان الذي كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r5.claim: Ibn Masud's reading places the polytheists before the People of the Book in the phrase.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r5.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : لم يكن المشركون وأهل الكتاب منفكين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r6.claim: The Messenger from God is Muhammad.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r7.claim: The purified pages refer to the Quran; alternatively, the Prophet's mission is followed by the descent of scriptures to earlier prophets.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r7.anchor: يعني القرآن . ويحتمل ثانيا : يتعقب بنبوته نزول الصحف

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r8.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r8.claim: One gloss of purified is free from shirk.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r9.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r9.claim: Another gloss of purified is that the pages' judgments are praised and commended.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r9.anchor: الثاني : مطهرة الحكم بحسن الذكر والثناء , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r10.claim: A further possibility is that the pages are purified because they descend from God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r10.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : لنزولها من عند الله .

MUQATIL:98:1-6/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r3.claim: The purified pages are the Book recited by Muhammad, called pages because it contains many kinds of qualities and is free of disbelief and polytheism; anything written can be called pages.
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r3.anchor: يعني يقرأ صحفا مطهرة، يعني كتابا لأنها جماعة فيها خصال كثيرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p351#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351#2/r1.claim: The messenger is Muhammad and stands in apposition to the clear proof; he recites papers or scrolls purified of falsehood.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351#2/r1.anchor: أى محمد عليه السلام وهو بدل من البينة

NAHHAS:v5p271/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r13.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v5p271/r13.claim: Al-Akhfash Saʿīd allows rasūlun min Allāh to be understood as 'it is a messenger from God.'
NAHHAS:v5p271/r13.anchor: على البدل ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى هي رسول من الله قال الأخفش سعيد

NAHHAS:v5p271/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r14.speaker: أبي
NAHHAS:v5p271/r14.claim: Ubayy's form rasūlan min Allāh is a circumstantial accusative.
NAHHAS:v5p271/r14.anchor: وفي حرف أبي ( رسولا من الله ) على الحال

NAHHAS:v5p271/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r15.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v5p271/r15.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the messenger as Muḥammad and the purified scrolls as the Qur'an.
NAHHAS:v5p271/r15.anchor: قال الضحاك الرسول محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ( يتلو صحفا مطهرة ) قال القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses rasul as an appositive to al-bayyina.

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r8.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r8.claim: Al-Farra reads the phrase as meaning that the proof is a messenger from God, since bayyina can be referred to as a person.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r8.anchor: الفراء: أي هي رسول من الله، أو هو رسول من الله لأن البينة قد تذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r9.claim: Ubayy's and Ibn Masud's codices have rasulan in the accusative as a detached accusative construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r9.anchor: وفي حرف أبي وابن مسعود «رسولا» بالنصب على القطع

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r10.claim: Yatlu means to read aloud, and suhuf is the plural of sahifa, the container of writing.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r10.anchor: يتلو } أي يقرأ. يقال: تلا يتلو تلاوة. { صحفا } جمع صحيفة، وهي ظرف المكتوب

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says the purified sheets are free of falsehood, doubt, hypocrisy, and error.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r11.anchor: مطهرة } قال ابن عباس: من الزور، والشك، والنفاق، والضلالة

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r12.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r12.claim: Qatada glosses the sheets as purified from falsehood; other glosses list lies, ambiguities, and unbelief, which Qurtubi says come to the same meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r12.anchor: وقال قتادة: من الباطل. وقيل: من الكذب، والشبهات، والكفر والمعنى واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r13.claim: The Prophet recited the written revelation from memory because he was unlettered, so the sheets signify their written content rather than a book he read.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r13.anchor: كان يتلو عن ظهر قلبه، لا عن كتاب لأنه كان أميا، لا يكتب ولا يقرأ

QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r1.claim: Although purified grammatically describes the sheets, it describes the Quranic content within them, as in 80:13–14.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r1.anchor: فالمطهرة نعت للصحف في الظاهر، وهي نعت لما في الصحف من القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r2.claim: Another interpretation says the sheets should be touched only by the purified, as discussed at 56:79.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r2.anchor: ينبغي ألا يمسها إلا المطهرون كما قال في سورة «الواقعة

QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r3.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the purified sheets are in heaven, in the Mother of the Book from which revealed scriptures were copied, linked to 85:21–22.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r3.anchor:
كما قال تعالى:
بل هو قرآن مجيد * في لوح محفوظ
[البروج: 21 22]. قال الحسن: يعني الصحف المطهرة في السماء. { فيها

QUTB-ZILAL:98:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:98:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:98:2/r1.claim: The Messenger comes from God and recites purified scriptures; the scriptures are purified of associating partners with God and unbelief.

RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r1.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r1.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Zayd take the proof as the Quran, citing 20:133; رسول من الله then has an omitted noun, meaning that proof is revelation and the Messenger recites purified sheets.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r1.anchor: القول الثالث : وهو قتادة وابن زيد : { البينة } هي القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r2.claim: Ṣuḥuf means sheets that contain writing; the adjective purified formally modifies the sheets but really describes the Quran they contain.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r2.anchor: الصحف جمع صحيفة وهي ظرف للمكتوب

RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r3.claim: One reading takes the purified sheets as exalted and protected from falsehood, like the Quran's immunity from falsehood in 41:42.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r3.anchor: مرفوعة مطهرة } عن الباطل وهي كقوله : { لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه }

RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r4.claim: Another reading says the Quran is purified of blameworthy mention because it receives the finest praise.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r4.anchor: مطهرة عن الذكر القبيح فإن القرآن يذكر بأحسن الذكر ويثني عليه أحسن الثناء

RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r5.claim: A third reading says only the ritually pure should touch the sheets, as in 56:79.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r5.anchor: أي ينبغي أن لا يمسها إلا المطهرون ، كقوله تعالى : { فى كتاب مكنون * لا يمسه إلا المطهرون }

RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r6.claim: كتب can mean the written verses in the sheets, or rulings, as صاحب النظم argues from كتب الله لأغلبن and the hadith invoking God's Book as His judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r6.anchor: قال صاحب النظم : الكتب قد يكون بمعنى الحكم : { كتب الله لاغلبن }

RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains qayyima as upright, without deviation, and as clarifying truth from falsehood; the root conveys standing or being established.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج : مستقيمة لا عوج فيها تبين الحق من الباطل

RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r8.claim: A second interpretation makes qayyima mean established and independently standing as proof, from the idiom of carrying through a matter.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r8.anchor: أن تكون القيمة بمعنى القائمة أي هي قائمة مستقلة بالحجة والدلالة

RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r9.claim: Although Muhammad was unlettered, reciting what is written in the sheets counts as reciting their contents; a book attributed to Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says he could read but not write, perhaps miraculously.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r9.anchor: إذا تلا مثلا المسطور في تلك الصحف كان تاليا ما فيها

SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r1.claim: Rasūl may be a nominative appositive to al-bayyinah, either apposition of inclusion or whole-to-whole hyperbole, or with an omitted noun meaning the Messenger's proof; it may also predicate an omitted hiya.
SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r1.anchor: العامة على رفعه بدلا من " البينة ": إما بدل اشتمال، وإما كل من كل على سبيل المبالغة

SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r2.speaker: عبد الله، أبي
SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy read rasūlan in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase from al-bayyinah, preserving the same hyperbole or ellipsis.
SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأبي " رسولا " على الحال من البينة

SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r3.claim: Min Allāh may modify rasūl or describe it; Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows it to be a circumstantial modifier of the scrolls, understood as sent down from God.
SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r3.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء وجها ثالثا وهو: أن يكون حالا من " صحفا

SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:98:2/r4.claim: Yatlu may describe rasūl or be circumstantial to a pronoun in the preceding prepositional phrase if min Allāh is an adjective of rasūl.

STUDYQURAN:98:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r1.speaker: Bg, IK, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r1.claim: Most commentators take the purified scriptures as the Quran and the messenger as Muhammad.
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r1.anchor: The majority of commentators interpret scriptures purified as a reference to the Quran and a messenger as a reference to Muhammad

STUDYQURAN:98:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r2.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r2.claim: The messenger may instead be Gabriel.
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r2.anchor: Messenger can, however, also be read as a reference to the Archangel Gabriel

STUDYQURAN:98:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r3.claim: Both terms may refer more generally to the messengers and revelations sent to every community, each of which had a warner.
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r3.anchor: both terms could be seen as references to the messengers and revelations that each community has been sent

STUDYQURAN:98:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r4.speaker: Sh
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r4.claim: The purified scriptures may refer to the Preserved Tablet, from which revelation descends.
STUDYQURAN:98:2/r4.anchor: Scriptures purified can also be read as a reference to the Preserved Tablet

TAB:98:1/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:1/r9.speaker: author
TAB:98:1/r9.claim: The proof is the clarification that Muhammad is God’s messenger, who reads scriptures purified of falsehood; those scriptures contain God-given, just, upright books without error.
TAB:98:1/r9.anchor: ثم ترجم عن البيّنة ،   فقال :  تلك البينة {  رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفا مُطَهّرَةً } يقول :  يقرأ صحفا مطهرة من الباطل {  فِيها كُتُبٌ قَيّمَةٌ } يقول :  في الصحف

TAB:98:1/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:1/r10.speaker: قتادة
TAB:98:1/r10.claim: Qatadah says the Messenger recounts and praises the Qur’an in the finest way.
TAB:98:1/r10.anchor: عن قتادة {  رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفا مُطَهّرَةً } يذكر القرآن بأحسن الذكر ،   ويثني عليه بأحسن الثناء

TAB:98:3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:3/r9.speaker: author
TAB:98:3/r9.claim: The proof is the clarification that Muhammad is God’s messenger, who reads scriptures purified of falsehood; those scriptures contain God-given, just, upright books without error.
TAB:98:3/r9.anchor: ثم ترجم عن البيّنة ،   فقال :  تلك البينة {  رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفا مُطَهّرَةً } يقول :  يقرأ صحفا مطهرة من الباطل {  فِيها كُتُبٌ قَيّمَةٌ } يقول :  في الصحف

TAB:98:3/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:3/r10.speaker: قتادة
TAB:98:3/r10.claim: Qatadah says the Messenger recounts and praises the Qur’an in the finest way.
TAB:98:3/r10.anchor: عن قتادة {  رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفا مُطَهّرَةً } يذكر القرآن بأحسن الذكر ،   ويثني عليه بأحسن الثناء

TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that unbelievers were not divided over Muhammad until God sent him as Messenger; afterward some denied and some believed, though before his mission they agreed he was a prophet.
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r5.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصحة أن يقال: معنى ذلك: لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين مفترقين في أمر محمد

TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r7.claim: “A Messenger from God” is indefinite in apposition to the definite proof, as in the verse describing the Lord of the Throne as glorious.
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r7.anchor: واستؤنف قوله {رسول من الله} [البينة: 2] وهي نكرة على البينة، وهي معرفة، كما قيل: {ذو العرش المجيد فعال} [البروج: 16]

TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r8.claim: The proof clarifies Muhammad’s messengership; he recites pages purified of falsehood, containing just, upright divine teachings without error.
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r8.anchor: ثم ترجم عن البينة، فقال: تلك البينة، {رسول من الله يتلو صحفا مطهرة} [البينة: 2] ، يقول: يقرأ صحفا مطهرة من الباطل

TAB-FULL:v24p553/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p553/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p553/r1.claim: Qatada says the Messenger presents the Qur’an with the finest remembrance and praise.
TAB-FULL:v24p553/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {رسول من الله يتلو صحفا مطهرة} [البينة: 2] «يذكر القرآن بأحسن الذكر، ويثني عليه بأحسن الثناء»

TABATABAI:98:1-3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r3.claim: The messenger reciting purified pages is certainly Muhammad; ṣuḥuf are sheets and here the revealed portions of the Qur’an, as elsewhere in scripture language.
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r3.anchor: المراد به محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قطعا

TABATABAI:98:1-3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r4.claim: The pages are purified of falsehood touched by devils; God repeatedly says revelation is truth protected from their intrusion.
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r4.anchor: تقدسها من قذارة الباطل بمس الشياطين

TABRISI:98:1/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:1/r6.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:98:1/r6.claim: In the syntax, 'a messenger from God' may be an apposition explaining the preceding proof, or al-Farra treats it as a new sentence with an implied 'he'.
TABRISI:98:1/r6.anchor: رسول من الله بدل من البينة قبله

TABRISI:98:1-4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:1-4/r3.speaker: الحسن والجبائي
TABRISI:98:1-4/r3.claim: The purified pages are pure in heaven, touched only by purified angels, and Muhammad delivered them as the Quran, calling people to monotheism and faith.
TABRISI:98:1-4/r3.anchor: يعني مطهرة في السماء لا يمسها إلا الملائكة المطهرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r3.claim: The clear proof is Muḥammad; Muqātil says he explained their error and polytheism.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r3.anchor: وقوله: {البينة} هو قال ابن عبا لهم س: يريد محمدا -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r4.claim: Bayyina is manifest evidence distinguishing truth from falsehood; the Prophet, a just witness, or any proof may be called bayyina.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r4.anchor: ومعنى {البينة}: الحجة الظاهرة التي يتميز بها الحق من الباطل، # فالنبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- بينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r5.claim: The disbelievers had not left unbelief and polytheism until Muḥammad came with the Qurʾān, exposed their error, and called them to faith; this describes God's favor and concerns those from both groups who believed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r5.anchor: ومعنى الآية: إخبار الله تعالى عن الكفار أنهم لم (¬3) ينتهوا عن كفرهم وشركهم بالله حتى أتاهم محمد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r6.claim: “A messenger from God” is an appositive explaining the definite “clear proof.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: رسول: رفع على البدل من البينة، والتفسير لها (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats the indefinite “messenger” as a fresh nominative rather than an appositive to the definite “clear proof.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء: "رسول" نكرة استؤنف على البينة، وهي معرفة كما قال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r1.claim: The pages qualify the Messenger; ṣuḥuf is plural of ṣaḥīfa, the container for written material. He recites their contents from memory because he is unlettered.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r1.anchor: هذا من نعت الرسول، والصحف جمع صحيفة، وهي ظرف للمكتوب.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r2.claim: Muṭahhara means purified of lies, falsehood, doubt, hypocrisy, error, and ambiguities.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يريد من الكذب، والزور، والشك، والنفاق، والضلال، والشبهات (¬8).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r3.claim: Muqātil says the pages are purified of unbelief and polytheism.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the pages are purified of falsehood, as in 41:42 and 80:14.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p210/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي هي مطهرة من الباطل (¬11). يدل على # هذا قوله: {لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه}

WAHIDI-QT:98:2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:98:2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:98:2/r1.claim: The proof is a messenger from God who recites books purified of falsehood.
WAHIDI-QT:98:2/r1.anchor: ثم فسر البينة فقال { رسول من الله يتلو صحفا } كتبا { مطهرة } من الباطل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r4.claim: The messenger recites scriptures purified of falsehood.

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r12.claim: The bayyina is the Messenger from God, either by apposition or as an explanation of bayyina through an omitted subject and predicate.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r12.anchor: Allah tarafından risaletle gönderilmiş bir peygamber gelinceye kadar infikâk edecek değillerdi

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r13.claim: The purified sheets are free of distortion, suspicion, error, and false doubt, untouched by impure hands; he links them to other Qur’anic descriptions.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r13.anchor: mutahhar, yani tahriften, töhmetten, yanlışlıktan, bâtıl şüphesinden ârî, kirli eller dokunmaz

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.claim: Before a messenger, people could not fully know or unite upon true monotheism and could be excused; after the proof came, the People of the Book had no excuse for persisting in disbelief.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.anchor: öyle bir beyyine gelmedikçe tamamen hak ve tevhid dinini bilip de birleşecek ve hâllerini değiştirecek bir vaziyette bulunmuyorlardı ve bunda mâzur olabilirlerdi

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.claim: Razi frames the puzzle: if munfakkin means leaving disbelief and hatta marks an endpoint, the first verse implies conversion after the Messenger, while verse 4 says division followed the proof.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.anchor: Sonra infikâkleri ne şeyden, Allah teâlâ onu zikretmemiştir. Lâkin murad, bulundukları küfür hâlinden demek olduğu mâlumdur

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.claim: The preferred Keşşaf solution reads verse 1 as the disbelievers’ earlier pledge to stay in their religions until the promised Prophet Muhammad came; verse 4 reports their failure to keep that pledge.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.anchor: Birincisi ve en güzeli Sâhib-Keşşâf’ın telhis ettiği vecihtir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.claim: On that reading, they promised to unite in truth when the Prophet came but instead split and persisted in disbelief; Razi illustrates this with a sinner who increases sin after becoming rich.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.anchor: onlar o Peygamber geldiği zaman hak üzerinde ittifak ile bir kelimede toplanmak vaad ediyorlardı, sonra da haktan asıl ayrılmaları ve küfürde kararları o Resul gelince oldu

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.claim: A third proposal makes munfakkin refer to mentioning the coming Messenger’s virtues: they spoke of his merits before his arrival, then disagreed after he came.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.anchor: Üçüncüsü: Münfekkîn küfürden infikâke değil, beyyine olarak gelecek resûlün menâkıb ve fezâilini anmaktan[^12] infikâk etmedikleri mânasına olmalıdır

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.claim: A fourth proposal says that, after the Messenger came, the whole group no longer remained disbelieving because some believed and some did not, satisfying hatta’s implication of change.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.anchor: Çünkü mecmû‘u o küfürde kalmadılar, bazısı mü’min bazısı da kâfir oldular. Bu kadarı da ‘hattâ’nın medlûlüyle amele kâfîdir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.claim: A fifth proposal says the Prophet’s mission shook their prior certainty in inherited religions; some converted, while others divided through stubbornness despite recognizing their old religions’ weakness.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.anchor: Resûlullah ba‘s olununca alışmış yapışmış oldukları eski dinleri hakkındaki cezm ü itikadları mütezelzil ve evvelki fikr ü kanaatleri perişan oldu

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.claim: This proposal distinguishes infikak as detachment from something once clung to from tafarruq as dispersion, showing how the post-Prophet condition differed from the prior one.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.anchor: bir şeyin bir şeyden infikâki ona yapışmış iken kopup ayrılması demektir. Tefrika da dağılmaktır

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.claim: Razi transmits these five solutions but identifies the first as preferred; the author finds Keşşaf’s wording more subtle and compatible with several proposals.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.anchor: Râzî bu beş vechi hikâye ve beyan etmiş olmakla beraber kavl-i muhtâr birinci vecih olduğunu da ihtar eylemiştir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.claim: Abu al-Su‘ud and others follow the first solution but supply the prior state as the object: their pledge and resolve to believe and follow the last Messenger.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.anchor: Ebussuud ve daha birçokları da Keşşâf’ın birinci vechi üzerinde yürümekle beraber “infikâk”in müte‘allakını mukaddemâ üzerinde bulundukları şey

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.claim: The account says the People of the Book prayed for victory through the last Prophet and threatened Arab opponents that they would defeat them with him; later polytheists may have adopted the claim.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.anchor: Ehl-i kitabdan bu vaadin vukū‘unda şüphe yoktur. Hatta onlar onunla Allah’tan fütûhât diliyorlar

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.claim: They asked the People of the Book whether Muhammad was the figure named in their scripture, yet after his arrival the People of the Book disbelieved and divided.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.anchor: Resûlullah hakkında gidip ehl-i kitaba soruyorlar

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.claim: The author finds his earlier explanation most apparent: before the decisive proof, people were in a state where they could not leave their inherited condition; after it, the People of the Book should have believed.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.anchor: bunu bu esas üzere, yani bulundukları hâlden infikâk mânasına olarak bâlâda îzah ettiğimiz diğer bir vech ile anlamak

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.claim: The pledge reading is awkward when extended to polytheists; reading the object as their religions or disbelief would imply they should depart from them, though the proof was sent for that purpose.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.anchor: Ancak bunu o vaad ve azm ile tefsir etmek Sûre-i Bakara âyetine muvâfık olsa da müşriklere teşmîli itibariyle biraz dolambaçlı geliyor

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.claim: Before Muhammad’s mission was a period of interruption when religions were corrupted, pagans and non-pagans mixed, and truth and falsehood could not be distinguished.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.anchor: Resûlullah’ın bi‘setinden önceki zaman dinlerin tahrif ve teşvîşe uğradığı müşrikle gayr-i müşrikin karıştığı

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.claim: Given the rule that punishment does not come before a messenger, the interval is an excuse period without responsibility; before decisive proof, the default is to leave people in their existing state.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.anchor: Fetret zamanları ise وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًۭا hükmüne[^22] nazaran mes’ûliyet teveccüh etmeyen bir mazeret zamanı demektir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.claim: Prophets are sent to illuminate truth and duty during such periods, distinguishing believers and disbelievers so accountability can apply.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.anchor: Ve beşeriyetin böyle hakk u bâtılı seçemeyecek bir fetret ve zulmet içinde kaldığı zamanlardır ki taraf-ı ilâhîden

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.claim: Following the previous surah’s account of revelation’s wisdom, this surah explains the pre-Prophetic interval: before Qur’an and Messenger the disbelievers could be excused, but after proof, especially the People of the Book’s rejection and division, they deserved punishment.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.anchor: Kur’ân’ın inzâliyle beyyine-i ilâhiye olan Resûlullah’ın bi‘setinden evvel ehl-i kitabdan ve müşriklerden bulunan kâfirler bulundukları hâllerinden ayrılmamakta mâzur olsalar da, hak dini beyan eden bu beyyine geldikten sonra

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r6.claim: The clear proof named in verse 1 is Muhammad, sent to recite the Qur'an's pure pages, free of lies, hypocrisy, doubt, error, and deviation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r6.anchor: “tertemiz sayfalar” ise Kur’an’ın sayfaları olup “tertemiz” nitelemesi, “yalan, nifak, şüphe, sapkınlık ve yanlışlık vb. kusurlardan arınmış sayfalar”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.claim: Al-Bayyinah complements al-Qadr: the Qur’an’s exaltedness is explained, and the People of the Book and Makkan idolaters rejected it from conceit, not genuine doubt, using demands for a sign as a pretext.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.anchor: conceit and arrogance which led them to this attitude

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r3.claim: The demanded sign is an angel sent directly by God, not a human messenger who claims revelation; the angel must recite pure pages.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r3.anchor: they wanted some angel directly sent by the Almighty who would read untouched and pure pages

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r4.claim: A ṣaḥīfah is a page; the opponents would not accept an angel merely reporting God’s messages but wanted them written and read aloud.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r4.anchor: whatever he brings in the name of God should be in fact written and read

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r5.claim: The pages’ purity means untouched by any human or jinn, with only God and angels having touched them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r5.anchor: Except for God and the angels no one among men and jinn should have touched them

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r2.claim: Most readers place rasūl in the nominative as an appositive to al-bayyina; Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read it in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: رسول بالرفع بدلا من البينة، وأبي وعبد الله: بالنصب حالا من البينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r3.claim: The purified pages are sheets or leaves purified from falsehood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r3.anchor: يتلوا صحفا: أي قراطيس، مطهرة من الباطل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r1.claim: “A messenger” is apposition to “the clear proof,” or a predicate to an omitted subject; the indefinite form magnifies him, and he is the Prophet Muhammad.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r1.anchor: رسول بدل منها بدل كل من كل أو خبر لمقدر أي هي رسول

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r2.claim: “From God” modifies the messenger and adds a further distinction, reinforcing the honor already conveyed by the indefinite form.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r2.anchor: وقوله سبحانه من الله في موضع الصفة له مفيد للفخامة الإضافية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r3.claim: “Reciting purified pages” may modify the messenger or be circumstantial for the pronoun in the preceding modifier.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى يتلوا صحفا مطهرة صفة له أو حال من الضمير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r2.claim: The Messenger himself may be the proof because his character reached a miraculous degree, as al-Ghazali argues; al-Busiri’s verse points to his knowledge despite illiteracy and orphanhood, and other miracles also qualify.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r2.anchor: كما قال الغزالي في المنقذ من الضلال وأشار إليه البوصيري بقوله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r3.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r3.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd report that the proof is the Qur’an, which clarifies truth or stands as a miracle establishing the claim.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالبينة القرآن لأنه مبين للحق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r4.claim: Other parses make “messenger” an appositive with an understood noun such as proof, revelation, miracle, or book; or a predicate with the recitation clause explaining the proof, an aside praising it, or a modifier meaning the Qur’an.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r4.anchor: ورسول عليه قيل بدل اشتمال أو بدل كل من كل أيضا بتقدير مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r5.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r5.claim: Ubayy and ʿAbd Allah read “rasulan” in the accusative as a circumstantial accusative describing the proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعبد الله رسولا بالنصب على الحالية من البينة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r6.claim: Pages are sheets of writing; purifying them is a metaphor for their freedom from falsehood, or a metaphorical image of purity, or a transferred description implying only the purified touch them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r6.anchor: والمراد بتطهيرها تنزيهها عن الباطل على سبيل الأستعارة المصرحة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r8.claim: The Prophet’s reciting pages despite being unable to read is a metonymy referring to the content he recites; other proposals supply “like pages” or use metaphor and the pages for their contents.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r8.anchor: ووصفه عليه الصلاة والسلام بتلاوة الصحف المذكورة بناء على المشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r9.claim: An alternative identifies the messenger as Gabriel and the pages as angelic copies from the Preserved Tablet, but turning “pages” into revelation is weak; al-Alusi prefers Muhammad, as reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r9.anchor: والأولى حمل الرسول على النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وهو المروي عن ابن عباس ومقاتل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r10.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r10.claim: Al-Wahidi calls the passage among the Qur’an’s hardest in structure and exegesis: reading it as pre-mission disbelief seems to say they stopped disbelieving when the Messenger came, contrary to what follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r10.anchor: حتى قال الواحدي في كتاب البسيط أنها من أصعب ما في القرآن نظما وتفسيرا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r4.claim: The purified pages are the Qur'an's written contents, which the Prophet recited from memory rather than from a book; purified means free of falsehood, lies, and fabrication.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r4.anchor: يريد ما يتضمنه الصحف من المكتوب فيها، وهو القرآن؛ لأنه كان يتلو عن ظهر قلبه لا عن [الكتاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.claim: The Prophet said God commanded him to recite this sura to Ubayy; when Ubayy asked whether he had been named, the Prophet said yes and Ubayy wept.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي: "إن الله تعالى أمرني أن أقرأ عليك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.claim: A variant from Qatada says the command was for the Prophet to recite the Qur'an to Ubayy.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.anchor: وقال همام عن قتادة: "أمرني أن أقرأ عليك القرآن

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r5.claim: Rasul min Allah may be an appositive to al-bayyina, directly or through an implied genitive, or it may begin a new nominal sentence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r5.anchor: بنفسه أو بتقدير مضاف أو مبتدأ

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r6.claim: Although unlettered, the Prophet is like one reciting the scrolls because he recited what they contain.
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r6.anchor: والرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام وإن كان أميا لكنه لما تلا مثل ما في الصحف كان كالتالي لها

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r7.claim: The Messenger reciting the scrolls may instead refer to Gabriel.
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r8.claim: The scrolls are purified because falsehood cannot reach their contents.
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r8.anchor: أن الباطل لا يأتي ما فيها

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r9.claim: The scrolls are purified because only the purified touch them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.claim: A report from the Prophet says that whoever recites this surah will be with the best of creation at the evening resting place on Judgment Day.
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة لم يكن الذين كفروا كان يوم القيامة مع خير البرية مساء ومقيلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r3.claim: Ṣuḥuf literally means sheets or paper, but here denotes their contents because of their close association.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r3.anchor: جمع صحيفة وهي القرطاس والمراد ما فيها , عبر بها عنه لشدة المواصلة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r4.claim: The pages are purified from idolatry and every deviation; falsehood cannot approach them, and only the purified touch them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r4.anchor: الباطل من الشرك بالأوثان وغيرها من كل زيغ لا يأتيها من بين يديها ولا من خلفها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r5.claim: Although unlettered, the Messenger's recitation counts as reading what is contained in the pages.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r5.anchor: وقراءته وإن كان أميا لمثل ما فيها قراءة لها

DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.claim: Ubayy reported that God ordered the Prophet to recite the opening of al-Bayyina to him, followed by statements identifying the true religion as non-polytheist hanifiyya and promising that good is not denied.
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.anchor: إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك فقرأ علي

DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.claim: A second Ubayy report presents an expanded recitation with explanations of upright religion, righteous deeds, the best and worst of creation, and the recompense of the God-fearing.
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.anchor: إن أقوم الدين الحنيفية مسلمة غير مشركة

DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas recalled the Prophet's saying that Adam would seek a third valley of gold after two, and that only dust fills his belly; God accepts repentance.
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.anchor: لو كان لابن آدم واديان من ذهب لابتغى الثالث

DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.claim: Ubayy affirmed that the Prophet had taught him the disputed wording; Umar asked whether to enter it in the codex, and Ubayy did not forbid him.
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.anchor: هكذا اقرأنيها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, Ubayy quoted the two-valley saying, and Umar asked whether it should be written; Ubayy said he would not forbid it, while remaining unsure whether it was revelation or Prophetic speech.
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.anchor: فكأن أبيا شك أقول من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو قرآن منزل

DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.claim: Qatada glossed منفكين as ceasing their state, the Bayyina as this Qur'an, and the purified pages as the Qur'an praised in the finest terms.
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين} قال: منتهي عما هم فيه

IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r1.speaker: سكين وعدي بن زيد
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports Sakeen and Adi ibn Zayd's claim that God had sent no revelation to anyone after Moses.
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r1.anchor: وقال سكين وعدي بن زيد: يا محمد، ما نعلم أن الله أنزل على بشر من شيء بعد موسى

IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says God answered by recounting revelation to Muhammad as to earlier prophets, naming later prophets and explaining that messengers brought warning and good news so people would have no argument against God after their coming.
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r2.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى في ذلك من قولهما: إنا أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح والنبيين من بعده

IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r3.speaker: جماعة منهم
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r3.claim: A group told the Prophet they did not know he was God's messenger and would not testify to it, although he said they knew; Ibn Ishaq reports God's answer that He and the angels witness the revelation.
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r3.anchor: ودخلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جماعة منهم، فقال لهم: أما والله إنكم لتعلمون أني رسول من الله إليكم

IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r4.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r4.claim: The Qur'anic response to their denial is that God testifies to what He revealed to Muhammad, sent with His knowledge, and that the angels also bear witness.
IBNHISHAM:v1p562#2/r4.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى في ذلك من قولهم: لكن الله يشهد بما أنزل إليك أنزله بعلمه والملائكة يشهدون، وكفى بالله شهيدا

ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r1.claim: The majority read rasūl in the nominative as an apposition to al-bayyina.
ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { رسول } بالرفع بدلاً من { البينة }

ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r2.speaker: أبيّ وعبد الله
ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r2.claim: Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read rasūl in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of al-bayyina.
ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r2.anchor: وأبيّ وعبد الله : بالنصب حالاً من البينة

ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān glosses ṣuḥuf as sheets or scrolls and muṭahhara as free from falsehood.
ABUHAYYAN:98:2/r3.anchor: { يتلو صحفاً } : أي قراطيس ، { مطهرة } من الباطل

ALUSI:98:2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:2/r1.claim: Rasūl is either a complete apposition to al-bayyina or the predicate of an omitted subject meaning 'it is a Messenger'; its indefinite form magnifies him, and min Allah adds grandeur.
ALUSI:98:2/r1.anchor: بدل منها بدل كل من كل أو خبر لمقدر أي هي رسول وتنوينه للتفخيم

ALUSI:98:2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:2/r2.claim: The phrase 'from God' modifies Messenger and adds honor by relation, reinforcing the grandeur inherent in the indefinite noun.

ALUSI:98:2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:2/r3.claim: The recitation clause is either another adjective of Messenger or a circumstantial clause attached to the pronoun in the first adjective.
ALUSI:98:2/r3.anchor: صفة أخرى له أو حال من الضمير في صفته الأولى

ALUSI:98:3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:3/r2.claim: If bayyina means the Prophet who clarifies truth, identifying the proof with him is straightforward; if it means proof, his qualities are miraculous, as al-Ghazali and al-Busiri indicate, alongside other manifest miracles.
ALUSI:98:3/r2.anchor: وإطلاق البينة عليه عليه الصلاة والسلام على المعنى الأول ظاهر وعلى المعنى الأخير باعتبار أن أخلاقه وصفاته

ALUSI:98:3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r3.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
ALUSI:98:3/r3.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd are reported to take al-bayyina as the Qur'an, because it clarifies truth or is a miraculous proof establishing the claim.
ALUSI:98:3/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالبينة القرآن لأنه مبين للحق أو معجز مثبت للمدعي وروي ذلك عن قتادة وابن زيد

ALUSI:98:3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:3/r4.claim: If bayyina means Qur'an, rasūl may be an apposition with an omitted noun such as proof, revelation, miracle, or book of a Messenger, or a predicate with such a noun understood.
ALUSI:98:3/r4.anchor: عليه قيل بدل اشتمال أو بدل كل من كل أيضاً بتقدير مضاف أي بينة أو وحي أو معجز

ALUSI:98:3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:3/r5.claim: Other analyses make rasūl the subject with yatlū as predicate, explaining al-bayyina, interrupting to praise it, or modifying al-bayyina understood as the Qur'an.
ALUSI:98:3/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يكون رسول مبتدأ لوصفه وخبره جملة

ALUSI:98:3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r6.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
ALUSI:98:3/r6.claim: Ubayy and Abdullah read rasūlan in the accusative as a circumstantial accusative from al-bayyina.
ALUSI:98:3/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعبد الله رسولاً بالنصب على الحالية من البينة

ALUSI:98:3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:3/r7.claim: Ṣuḥuf is a plural of ṣaḥīfa, like ṣuḥāf, meaning writing sheets; its root conveys something spread out.
ALUSI:98:3/r7.anchor: والصحف جمع صحيفة وكذا الصحاف القراطيس التي يكتب فيها وأصلها المبسوط

ALUSI:98:3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:3/r8.claim: Purified may mean protected from falsehood by explicit metaphor, or pages touched only by ritually pure people, with the attribution made figuratively.
ALUSI:98:3/r8.anchor: والمراد بتطهيرها تنزيهها عن الباطل على سبيل الاستعارة المصرحة

ALUSI:98:3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:3/r10.claim: Though the Prophet famously neither read nor wrote, saying he recites the pages transfers the action to its object: by reciting their contents it is as if he read the sheets.
ALUSI:98:3/r10.anchor: بناء على المشهور من أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يكن يقرأ الكتاب كما أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يكن يكتب

ALUSI:98:3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:3/r11.claim: Other explanations posit an omitted 'like' before pages, an implicit metaphor comparing the Prophet to a reader of their contents, or ṣuḥuf as a metonym for contents.
ALUSI:98:3/r11.anchor: وقيل على تقدير مضاف أي مثل صحف وقيل في ضمير يتلو استعارة مكنية

ALUSI:98:3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r12.speaker: بعض
ALUSI:98:3/r12.claim: Some take the Messenger as Gabriel and the purified pages as angelic copies from the Preserved Tablet; Al-Ālūsī rejects this and prefers Muhammad, as reported from Ibn Abbas, Muqatil, and others.
ALUSI:98:3/r12.anchor: وقيل المراد بالرسول جبريل عليه السلام وبالصحف صحف الملائكة عليهم السلام المنتسخة من اللوح المحفوظ

ALUSI:98:3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r13.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI:98:3/r13.claim: Al-Wahidi calls this one of the Qur'an's hardest passages in syntax and interpretation: if both groups disbelieved before the mission, the apparent sense says the Messenger's arrival ended their disbelief, contrary to history and 98:4, which says the people of the Book split only after the proof came.
ALUSI:98:3/r13.anchor: حتى قال الواحدي في كتاب البسيط أنها من أصعب ما في القرآن نظماً وتفسيراً

MUSNAD-AHMAD:21202/r2.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21202/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21202/r2.claim: In a second version, Ubayy reports the Prophet's recitation of verses 1–2, followed by statements that true religion is upright monotheism, good is rewarded, and human desire remains unsated.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21202/r2.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، قال: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك

BAGHAWI:98:2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:98:2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:98:2/r1.claim: The clear proof is a messenger from God who recites.
BAGHAWI:98:2/r1.anchor: ثم فسر البينة فقال :{ رسول من الله يتلو } يقرأ

BAGHAWI:98:2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:98:2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:98:2/r2.claim: Ṣuḥuf means books, or their written contents, which is the Quran; the Prophet recited it from memory rather than from a physical book.
BAGHAWI:98:2/r2.anchor: { صحفا } كتباً ، يريد ما يتضمنه الصحف من المكتوب فيها ، وهو القرآن ، لأنه كان يتلو عن ظهر قلبه

BAGHAWI:98:2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:98:2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:98:2/r3.claim: The pages are purified of falsehood, lies, and forgery.
BAGHAWI:98:2/r3.anchor: قوله : { مطهرة } من الباطل والكذب والزور

BAYDAWI:98:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:98:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:98:2/r1.claim: “A Messenger from God” may be an apposition to bayyina directly or through an implied noun, or may begin a new nominal sentence; yatlū may be its adjective or predicate.
BAYDAWI:98:2/r1.anchor: { رسول من الله } بدل من البينة بنفسه ، أو بتقدير مضاف ، أو مبتدأ { يتلو صحفا مطهرة } صفته أو خبره ،

BAYDAWI:98:2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:98:2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:98:2/r2.claim: Although unlettered, the Prophet is like a reader of the pages because he recites what they contain.
BAYDAWI:98:2/r2.anchor: والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن كان أميا لكنه لما تلا مثل ما في الصحف كان كالتالي لها

BAYDAWI:98:2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:98:2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:98:2/r3.claim: An alternative is that the messenger meant is Gabriel.
BAYDAWI:98:2/r3.anchor: وقيلّ : المراد جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام ،

BAYDAWI:98:2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:98:2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:98:2/r4.claim: The pages are purified either because falsehood cannot enter their contents or because only the purified may touch them.
BAYDAWI:98:2/r4.anchor: وكون الصحف مطهرة أن الباطل لا يأتي ما فيها ، أو أنها لا يمسها إلا المطهرون .

BIQAI:98:2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:2/r1.claim: The phrase clarifies the proof as an exceptionally eminent Messenger sent from God, possessor of majesty and generosity.
BIQAI:98:2/r1.anchor: ولذلك أبدل منها قوله : { رسول } أي عظيم جداً

BIQAI:98:2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:2/r2.claim: He recites with a mass-transmitted reading after God has taught him.
BIQAI:98:2/r2.anchor: أي يقرأ قراءة متواترة ، ذلك الرسول بعد تعليمنا له

BIQAI:98:2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:2/r3.claim: Ṣuḥuf are sheets or pages; the word stands for what is written in them because the physical page and its contents are closely connected.
BIQAI:98:2/r3.anchor: جمع صحيفة وهي القرطاس والمراد ما فيها

BIQAI:98:2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:2/r4.claim: The pages are wholly pure and free of filth, shirk, and deviation; falsehood cannot approach them from either direction, and only the purified touch them.
BIQAI:98:2/r4.anchor: بأن الباطل من الشرك بالأوثان وغيرها من كل زيغ لا يأتيها من بين يديها ولا من خلفها

BIQAI:98:2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:2/r5.claim: Biqāʿī also says the pages are touched only by the purified, echoing the Qurʾānic wording elsewhere.

BIQAI:98:2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:2/r6.claim: Although unlettered, the Prophet’s recitation of the contents counts as reciting the pages themselves.
BIQAI:98:2/r6.anchor: وقراءته وإن كان أمياً لمثل ما فيها قراءة لها

DURR:98:1/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r18.speaker: قتادة
DURR:98:1/r18.claim: Qatada says the messenger recounts the Qur'an with the finest remembrance and praises it in the finest terms.
DURR:98:1/r18.anchor: عن قتادة { لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين } قال : منتهين عما هم فيه

IBNASHUR:98:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r1.claim: The preceding discussion is set up as a prelude to the description of the messenger who recites purified pages.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r1.anchor: وقد جعل ذلك تمهيداً وتوطئة لقوله بعده :  { رسول من الله

IBNASHUR:98:2/r29.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r29.speaker: الفراء
IBNASHUR:98:2/r29.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows a stop at “until the proof comes”; “a messenger from God” then begins an explanatory sentence, “it is a messenger from God,” parenthetically placed before 98:4.

IBNASHUR:98:2/r30.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r30.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r30.claim: Alternatively, rasūl may be an apposition to al-bayyina, continuing the earlier phrase and presenting their expected proof as the messenger who had already come.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r30.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { رسول } بدلاً من { البينة }

IBNASHUR:98:2/r31.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r31.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r31.claim: On the appositional reading, the verse defeats their excuses: the awaited proof has arrived, but they do not reflect, act fairly, or understand, as in the Jews’ earlier rejection.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r31.anchor: أريد إبطال معاذيرهم وإقامة الحجة عليهم بأن البينة التي ينتظرونها قد حلت ولكنهم لا يتدبرون أو لا ينصفون أو لا يفقهون

IBNASHUR:98:2/r32.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r32.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r32.claim: The indefinite rasūl marks a type and makes the awaited matter easier to accept, as in “numbered days” and the description “alif lām mīm ṣād, a Book.”
IBNASHUR:98:2/r32.anchor: للنوعية المرادِ منها تيسير ما يستصعب

IBNASHUR:98:2/r33.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r33.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r33.claim: The wording declares that the proof has arrived and identifies it as the messenger, paralleling the declaration that a warner and bringer of good news has now come.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r33.anchor: وفي هذا التبيين إبطال لمعاذيرهم كأنه قيل : فقد جاءتكم البينة ، على حد قوله تعالى : { أن تقولوا ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير فقد جاءكم بشير ونذير }

IBNASHUR:98:2/r34.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r34.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r34.claim: The identification of the proof with the messenger resembles the verse describing God as having sent down a Reminder, a messenger reciting God’s signs.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r34.anchor: وهو يفيد أن البينة هي الرسول وذلك مثل قوله تعالى : { قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكراً رسولاً يتلو عليكم آيات الله }

IBNASHUR:98:2/r35.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r35.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r35.claim: The reply mirrors the polytheists’ escalating demands for impossible signs and a written book, answered by affirming that the Prophet is a human messenger.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r35.anchor: فأسلوب هذا الرد مثل أسلوب قوله تعالى : { وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعاً أو تكون لك جنة من نخيل وعنب

IBNASHUR:98:2/r36.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r36.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r36.claim: Their own scriptures promised a messenger bearing a law and confirming prior scripture, speaking God’s revelation; this is reflected in the Torah and Gospel quotations and in the Qur’an’s description of confirmation.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r36.anchor: وفي هذا تذكير بغلطهم فإن كتبهم ما وعدت إلا بمجيء رسول معه شريعة وكتاب مصدق لما بين يديه وذلك مما يندرج في قولة التوراة

IBNASHUR:98:2/r37.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r37.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r37.claim: The Torah and Gospel characterized the promised prophet as like Moses or Jesus: a messenger given a law, conveying revelation from God, whose sign is truthfulness.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r37.anchor: لأن التوراة والإنجيل لم يصفا النبي الموعود به

IBNASHUR:98:2/r38.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r38.speaker: حجة الإسلام
IBNASHUR:98:2/r38.claim: Al-Ghazālī writes in The Deliverer from Error that the Prophet’s virtuous character reached the miraculous and his miracles were exceptionally manifest and numerous.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r38.anchor: قال حجة الإسلام في كتاب « المنقذ من الضلال » : « إن مجموع الأخلاق الفاضلة كان بالغاً في نبينا إلى حد الإعجاز وأن معجزاته كانت غاية في الظهور والكثرة »

IBNASHUR:98:2/r39.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r39.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r39.claim: Min Allāh is attached to rasūl; avoiding an iḍāfa permits tanwīn on rasūl, which conveys the messenger’s exalted status.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r39.anchor: و { من الله } متعلق ب { رسول } ولم يسلك طريق الإضافة ليتأتى تنوين { رسول } فيشعر بتعظيم هذا الرسول

IBNASHUR:98:2/r40.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r40.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r40.claim: The clause “reciting pages” can be a second adjective or a circumstantial clause; it also inserts praise of the Qur’an, since earlier scriptures apparently did not describe the promised messenger this way.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r40.anchor: القرآن إذ الظاهر أن الرسول الموعود به في كتبهم لم يوصف

IBNASHUR:98:2/r41.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r41.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r41.claim: Tilāwa is to repeat speech without addition or omission, whether the speech is written or memorized; the verb signals the unchanged wording of revealed recitation.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r41.anchor: والتلاوة : إعادة الكلام دون زيادة عليه ولا نقص منه سواء كان كلاماً مكتوباً أو محفوظاً عن ظهر قلب

IBNASHUR:98:2/r42.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r42.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r42.claim: Ṣuḥuf are sheets or writing materials, including parchment, leather, or rags.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r42.anchor: والصحف : الأوراق والقراطيس التي تجعل لأن يكتب فيها ، وتكون من رق أو جلد ، أو من خرق

IBNASHUR:98:2/r43.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r43.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r43.claim: Calling the recited revelation ṣuḥuf is a metaphor by eventual outcome: it is commanded to be written and will become pages, like Joseph’s “I see myself pressing wine.”
IBNASHUR:98:2/r43.anchor: وتسمية ما يتلوه الرسول { صحفاً } مجاز بعلاقة الأيلولة لأنه مأمور بكتابته فهو عند تلاوته سيكون صحفاً

IBNASHUR:98:2/r44.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r44.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r44.claim: The wording indicates that God ordered the Qur’an written on sheets and similar materials, including sheep shoulder blades, rags, and stones; this also explains calling revelation a Book.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r44.anchor: وهذا إشارة إلى أن الله أمر رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بكتابة القرآن

IBNASHUR:98:2/r45.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r45.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r45.claim: Making yatlū govern ṣuḥuf is a familiar metonymy approaching literal usage, with the written object understood as what is read.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r45.anchor: وتعدية فعل { يتلو } إلى { صحفاً } مجاز مرسل مشهور ساوى الحقيقة

IBNASHUR:98:2/r46.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r46.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r46.claim: The Prophet recited the Qur’an from memory rather than reading pages; the phrase therefore means that he recited what was written in pages, as his well-known unlettered state makes clear.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r46.anchor: وإنما كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتلو عليهم القرآن عن ظهر قلب ولا يقرأه من صحف فمعنى { يتلو صحفاً } يتلو ما هو مكتوب في صحف والقرينة ظاهرة وهي اشتهار كونه صلى الله عليه وسلم أمياً

IBNASHUR:98:2/r47.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r47.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r47.claim: The pages’ purity is figurative: their meanings are clear and contain no misleading material, implicitly contrasting them with distortions and delusions in some People of the Book’s scriptures.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r47.anchor: ووصف الصحف ب { مطهرة } وهو وصف مشتق من الطهارة المجازية ، أي كون معانيه لا لبس فيها ولا تشتمل على ما فيه تضليل

IBNASHUR:98:2/r48.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r48.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r48.claim: Kutub is the plural of kitāb, a verbal noun meaning something written; the books within the pages are the Qur’an.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r48.anchor: والكتب : جمع كتاب ، وهو فعال اسم بمعنى المكتوب ، فمعنى كون الكتب كائنة في الصحف

IBNASHUR:98:2/r49.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r49.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r49.claim: The Qur’an written on the pages contains the uncorrupted truth of earlier scriptures; it confirms prior scripture and gathers the essence and fruit of the earlier books.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r49.anchor: أن الصحف التي يكتب فيها القرآن تشتمل على القرآن وهو يشتمل على ما تضمنته كتب الرسل السابقين مما هو خالص من التحريف والباطل

IBNASHUR:98:2/r50.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r50.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r50.claim: Calling the Qur’an’s yield from previous scriptures “books” is a part-for-whole metaphor that names the fruit of those books as books themselves.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r50.anchor: فالقرآن زبدة ما في الكتب الأولى ومجمع ثمرتها ، فأطلق على ثمرة الكتب اسم كتب على وجه مجاز الجزئية

IBNASHUR:98:2/r51.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r51.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r51.claim: The books meant here are the portions of the Qur’an, namely its sūras.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r51.anchor: والمراد بالكتب أجزاء القرآن أو سوره فهي بمثابة الكتب

IBNATIYYA:98:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r1.claim: The majority read rasūlun, with the word in the nominative.
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { رسول من الله } بالرفع

IBNATIYYA:98:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r2.speaker: أبي
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r2.claim: Ubayy reads rasūlan in the accusative as a circumstantial accusative.
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبي : { رسولاً } بالنصب على الحال

IBNATIYYA:98:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r3.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda say the purified pages are the Qurʾān in its written pages.
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r3.anchor: والصحف المطهرة : القرآن في صحفه ،   قاله الضحاك وقتادة

IBNATIYYA:98:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the purified pages are in heaven.
IBNATIYYA:98:2/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن : والصحف المطهرة في السماء

IBNKATHIR:98:2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:98:2/r1.claim: The clear proof is Muhammad and the Qur’an he recites, inscribed in the highest assembly in purified pages; Ibn Kathīr links this to 80:13–16.
IBNKATHIR:98:2/r1.anchor: يعني : محمدًا صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وما يتلوه من القرآن العظيم

IBNKATHIR:98:3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:3/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:98:3/r2.claim: Qatāda says the Messenger recounts the Qur’an in the finest remembrance and praises it with the finest praise.
IBNKATHIR:98:3/r2.anchor: قال قتادة : { رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفًا مُطَهَّرَةً } يذكر القرآن بأحسن الذكر ، ويثني عليه بأحسن الثناء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir conjectures that the doubt Ubay experienced prompted the Prophet to recite Surah al-Bayyinah to him as reassurance, since it includes the Messenger reciting purified pages containing upright books.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.anchor: قلت: وهذا الشك الذي حصل لأبي في تلك الساعة هو، والله أعلم، السبب الذي لأجله قرأ عليه رسول الله

MAWARDI:98:2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:98:2/r1.claim: The messenger from God is Muhammad.

MAWARDI:98:2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:98:2/r2.claim: The purified pages recited by the messenger mean the Qurʾān.

MAWARDI:98:2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:98:2/r3.claim: Alternatively, Muhammad’s prophethood follows the revelation of purified scriptures to the prophets before him.
MAWARDI:98:2/r3.anchor: يتعقب بنبوته نزول الصحف المطهرة على الأنبياء قبله

MAWARDI:98:2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:2/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:98:2/r5.claim: Muṭahhara means purified in judgment and honored with good remembrance and praise.
MAWARDI:98:2/r5.anchor: الثاني : مطهرة الحكم بحسن الذكر والثناء ، قاله قتادة

MAWARDI:98:2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:98:2/r6.claim: A further possibility is that the pages are purified because they descend from God.
MAWARDI:98:2/r6.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : لنزولها من عند الله

NASAFI:98:2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:2/r1.claim: The messenger from God is Muhammad.
NASAFI:98:2/r1.anchor: أي محمد عليه السلام ، وهو بدل من { البينة }

NASAFI:98:2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:2/r2.claim: “A messenger from God” is an apposition to “the clear proof.”
NASAFI:98:2/r2.anchor: أي محمد عليه السلام ، وهو بدل من { البينة }

NASAFI:98:2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:2/r3.claim: The messenger recites the scriptures to them.
NASAFI:98:2/r3.anchor: { يَتْلُواْ } يقرأ عليهم { صُحُفاً } قراطيس { مُّطَهَّرَةٍ }

NASAFI:98:2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:2/r4.claim: The scriptures are sheets purified of falsehood.

QURTUBI:98:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:2/r1.claim: Rasul means an emissary sent by God.
