QURTUBI:98:2/r1.anchor: أي بعيث من الله جل ثناؤه .

QURTUBI:98:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI:98:2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses rasul as nominative in apposition to al-bayyina.
QURTUBI:98:2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : { رسول } رفع على البدل من  " البينة " .

QURTUBI:98:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:2/r3.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:98:2/r3.claim: Al-Farra reads the construction as either it is a messenger from God or he is a messenger from God, since bayyina can be spoken of as a person.
QURTUBI:98:2/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء : أي هي رسول من الله ، أو هو رسول من الله ؛ لأن البينة قد تذكر

QURTUBI:98:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:2/r4.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
QURTUBI:98:2/r4.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masud have rasulan in the accusative, as an independent or specification accusative.
QURTUBI:98:2/r4.anchor: وفي حرف أبي وابن مسعود { رسولا } بالنصب على القطع .

QURTUBI:98:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:2/r5.claim: Yatlu means to read or recite.
QURTUBI:98:2/r5.anchor: { يتلو } أي يقرأ . يقال : تلا يتلو تلاوة

QURTUBI:98:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:2/r6.claim: Suhuf is the plural of sahifa, the vessel or surface that holds writing.
QURTUBI:98:2/r6.anchor: { صحفا } جمع صحيفة ، وهي ظرف المكتوب .

QURTUBI:98:2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وغيرهما
QURTUBI:98:2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sheets are cleared of falsehood, doubt, hypocrisy, and error; Qatada says falsehood, and others add lies, ambiguities, and disbelief—the sense is the same.
QURTUBI:98:2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس : من الزور ، والشك ، والنفاق ، والضلالة . وقال قتادة : من الباطل

QURTUBI:98:2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:2/r8.claim: The Prophet recites the writing contained in the sheets from memory rather than from a physical book, since he was unlettered and neither wrote nor read.
QURTUBI:98:2/r8.anchor: أي يقرأ ما تتضمن الصحف من المكتوب ؛ ويدل عليه أنه كان يتلو عن ظهر قلبه ، لا عن كتاب

QURTUBI:98:2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:2/r9.claim: Though mutahhara grammatically modifies suhuf, it describes the Qur'an within them; compare the honored, elevated, purified sheets in 80:13–14.
QURTUBI:98:2/r9.anchor: و{ مطهرة } : من نعت الصحف ، وهو كقوله تعالى : { في صحف مكرمة . مرفوعة مطهرة }

QURTUBI:98:2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:2/r10.claim: Another view understands the sheets to be such that none should touch them except the purified, as discussed under 56:79.
QURTUBI:98:2/r10.anchor: أي ينبغي ألا يمسها إلا المطهرون ، كما قال في سورة

QURTUBI:98:2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:2/r11.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI:98:2/r11.claim: One view identifies the purified sheets as the heavenly original in Umm al-Kitab from which the revealed books were copied; al-Hasan says these sheets are in heaven, as in 85:21–22.
QURTUBI:98:2/r11.anchor: قال الحسن : يعني الصحف المطهرة في السماء .

RAZI:98:2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:98:2/r1.claim: Ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfa, a receptacle or surface for written material.
RAZI:98:2/r1.anchor: الصحف جمع صحيفة وهي ظرف للمكتوب

RAZI:98:2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:98:2/r2.claim: One explanation of purified is that the scriptures are free of falsehood, as 41:42 says and 80:14 describes them as elevated and purified.
RAZI:98:2/r2.anchor: لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه

RAZI:98:2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:98:2/r3.claim: Another explanation is that the Qur'an is purified from blameworthy mention and is instead praised in the finest terms.
RAZI:98:2/r3.anchor: مطهرة عن الذكر القبيح فإن القرآن يذكر بأحسن الذكر ويثني عليه أحسن الثناء

RAZI:98:2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:98:2/r4.claim: A third explanation is that the pages ought to be touched only by the ritually pure, as stated in 56:78–79.
RAZI:98:2/r4.anchor: ينبغي أن لا يمسها إلا المطهرون

RAZI:98:2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:98:2/r5.claim: Though grammatically an adjective of the pages, purified really describes the Qur'an contained in them.
RAZI:98:2/r5.anchor: وإن جرت نعتا للصحف في الظاهر فهي نعت لما في الصحف وهو القرآن

TAB:98:2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:2/r7.speaker: author
TAB:98:2/r7.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that the disbelievers were not divided over Muhammad until the proof came, meaning God sent him as Messenger to creation.
TAB:98:2/r7.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصحة أن يقال :  معنى ذلك :  لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين مفترقين في أمر محمد

TAB:98:2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:2/r9.speaker: author
TAB:98:2/r9.claim: “A Messenger from God” begins a new sentence and is indefinite while explaining the definite proof, like the Quranic wording about the glorious Throne and “effective.”
TAB:98:2/r9.anchor: واستؤنف قوله {  رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللّهِ } وهي نكرة على البيّنة ،   وهي معرفة ،   كما قيل :  {  ذُو الْعَرْشِ المَجِيدُ فَعّالٌ }

TAB:98:2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:2/r10.speaker: author
TAB:98:2/r10.claim: The proof is the Messenger sent by God, who recites pages purified of falsehood.
TAB:98:2/r10.anchor: ثم ترجم عن البيّنة ،   فقال :  تلك البينة {  رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفا مُطَهّرَةً } يقول :  يقرأ صحفا مطهرة من الباطل

TAB:98:2/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:2/r12.speaker: قتادة
TAB:98:2/r12.claim: Qatada says the Messenger mentions the Quran in the finest terms and praises it with the best praise.
TAB:98:2/r12.anchor: عن قتادة {  رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفا مُطَهّرَةً } يذكر القرآن بأحسن الذكر ،   ويثني عليه بأحسن الثناء .

BURHAN:v4p290/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p290/r9.speaker: author
